full_judgment:
3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint. Their case, in short, is that the disputed 'beel' is a big one comprising 9.12 acres of land and it is a natural one. The C.S. record was prepared in Khas Khatian No. 1 in the name of Zaminder Biddut Kumar Sarker and the plaintiff never possessed the suit land and they have no right and title in the suit land, And as such the suit for declaration of title is liable to be dismissed. 

 8. Mr. Md. Taherul Islam, learned Advocate-on-record, appearing on behalf of the leave-petitioner, submits that the High Court Division erroneously came to a finding that the petitioner is entitled to 8 annas share of the suit 'beel' as the C.S. Khatian No. 1176 was prepared in their names of their predecessors for payment of RjKi for fishing in the 'beel' although the plaintiffs took settlement of the suit 'beel' in raiyoti interest and as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside. He further submits that the High Court Division has made out a third case and that both the courts below also erroneously came to a finding that the plaintiff court not prove his title and possession in the suit 'beel' and as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside. 

 10. The High Court Division came to a finding that admittedly, the suit property is a 'beel' having an area of 9.12 acres of land and that the petitioner and his predecessors used to fish in the suit 'beel'. Having considered the materials on record and the evidence of the witnesses, the High Court Division found that it was proved that the suit property belonged to the Government which leased out the 'beel' to respondent No. 2, the Grameen Bank which is the view of the High Court Division was against the principle of natural justice. The high Court Division further found that P.W. 1 Shamsul Huq, deposed that on the basis of C.S. Khatian No. 1176, they paid RjKi in respect of 8 annas share of the suit 'beel' and that the C.S. record was accordingly prepared in their names. The High Court Division further found that the courts below failed to take decision impartially on consideration of facts and law and thereby committed error depriving the plaintiff who are private persons and that leasing out the suit 'beel' by respondent No. 1 to respondent No. 2 was malafide and the same deprived the petitioner from the suit land. Therefore, the High Court Division concluded that the petitioner should not be deprived from his claim of 8 annas share as deposed by P.W. 1 Shamsul Huq. 

 12. Having considered both C.S. and S.A. Khatians, bothe the court below found that the S.A. Khatian prepared subsequent to the C.S. Khatian was not prepared and published in the names of predecessors of the plaintiff. Both the courts below concurrently found that the plaintiff could not prove his title and possession in the suit 'beel'.
